description: Repo-scale (ruby-eventboard): canceling an event must cascade across the listing filter, #register, and #add_walk_in
prompts: Add `RsvpService#cancel_event(event_id)`, which marks the event's `canceled` field true (raise RsvpError if the event doesn't exist). Also add `RsvpService#add_walk_in(event_id:, attendee_id:)`: a direct-confirm registration for VIP walk-ins that bypasses the normal capacity/waitlist logic entirely (always creates a "confirmed" rsvp, with no waitlisting). Event cancellation must cascade across THREE places: (1) `EventRepository#all` gains an `include_canceled:` keyword arg (default false) that excludes canceled events unless true; (2) `#register` must raise RsvpError for a canceled event (it already checks the event exists - add the canceled check too); (3) `#add_walk_in` must ALSO raise RsvpError for a canceled event - both registration paths must respect cancellation, not just the normal one.

test_setup_files.test/event_cancellation_test.rb:
require_relative "test_helper"

class EventCancellationTest < Minitest::Test
  include EventBoardTestSetup

  def test_canceled_event_excluded_from_list_unless_included
    events, attendees, rsvps, service = build_service
    event = events.create(title: "Meetup", capacity: 5)
    service.cancel_event(event.id)

    assert_equal 0, events.all.length
    assert_equal 1, events.all(include_canceled: true).length
  end

  def test_canceled_event_rejects_register_and_walk_in
    events, attendees, rsvps, service = build_service
    event = events.create(title: "Meetup", capacity: 5)
    a1 = attendees.create(name: "A", email: "a@example.com")
    service.cancel_event(event.id)

    assert_raises(EventBoard::RsvpError) { service.register(event_id: event.id, attendee_id: a1.id) }
    assert_raises(EventBoard::RsvpError) { service.add_walk_in(event_id: event.id, attendee_id: a1.id) }
  end
end

module EventBoard
  class RsvpError < StandardError; end

  class RsvpService
    def initialize(events:, attendees:, rsvps:)
      @events = events
      @attendees = attendees
      @rsvps = rsvps
    end

    def register(event_id:, attendee_id:)
      event = @events.find(event_id)
      raise RsvpError, "event not found" unless event
      raise RsvpError, "event is canceled" if event.canceled?
      raise RsvpError, "attendee not found" unless @attendees.find(attendee_id)

      status = confirmed_count(event_id) < event.capacity ? "confirmed" : "waitlisted"
      @rsvps.create(event_id: event_id, attendee_id: attendee_id, status: status, created_at: Time.now.to_f)
    end

    def cancel(rsvp_id)
      rsvp = @rsvps.find(rsvp_id)
      raise RsvpError, "rsvp not found" unless rsvp
      raise RsvpError, "rsvp already canceled" if rsvp.status == "canceled"

      was_confirmed = rsvp.status == "confirmed"
      rsvp.status = "canceled"

      if was_confirmed
        next_waiting = @rsvps.for_event(rsvp.event_id).select { |r| r.status == "waitlisted" }.min_by(&:id)
        next_waiting.status = "confirmed" if next_waiting
      end

      rsvp
    end

    # Marks the event itself canceled - not to be confused with #cancel,
    # which cancels a single rsvp.
    def cancel_event(event_id)
      event = @events.find(event_id)
      raise RsvpError, "event not found" unless event

      event.canceled = true
      event
    end

    # A direct-confirm registration for VIP walk-ins, bypassing the normal
    # capacity/waitlist logic entirely - but it must still respect a
    # canceled event, same as the normal #register path.
    def add_walk_in(event_id:, attendee_id:)
      event = @events.find(event_id)
      raise RsvpError, "event not found" unless event
      raise RsvpError, "event is canceled" if event.canceled?
      raise RsvpError, "attendee not found" unless @attendees.find(attendee_id)

      @rsvps.create(event_id: event_id, attendee_id: attendee_id, status: "confirmed", created_at: Time.now.to_f)
    end

    private

    def confirmed_count(event_id)
      @rsvps.for_event(event_id).count { |r| r.status == "confirmed" }
    end
  end
end
